segments.say: Let your body settle where it is. Let your shoulders soften. Let your hands rest. There's nothing you need to do right now. Nothing to figure out. Your brain has been working hard all day, building a world for you. For a little while, it can rest.

Take a slow breath in. And let it out, even more slowly. Again. Breathe in, gently. And let it go. Notice how your breath moves all by itself. You don't need to control it. Your body knows how to breathe. It has been doing it all your life.

Now, if you like, notice the weight of your body. The places where it touches the bed, or the chair. Your heels. The backs of your legs. Your back. Your head. Let each of these places feel a little heavier. As if the surface beneath you is holding you completely, so you don't have to hold anything at all.

Remember the rubber hand? Your brain is always building the feeling of your body. Right now, let it build a feeling of softness. Warmth in your hands. Warmth in your feet. Heaviness in your arms. There's no need to make anything happen. Just notice, and let it be.

Think of your brain, for a moment, as a kind and tireless friend. All day long, it filled in the gaps for you. It guessed, and predicted, and told you stories so that the world would make sense. Now you can thank it, quietly, and let it rest. It has done enough for today.

If thoughts come, that's alright. Thoughts are just the brain doing what it does. Little predictions. Little stories. You don't need to follow them. Imagine them as clouds drifting across a night sky. You can notice a cloud, and then let it pass. And then the next one. And the sky stays calm behind them.

Maybe one of those clouds looks like a face. That's alright too. Your brain loves patterns. Let it play. You can smile at the shape, and let it drift away, slowly, toward the edge of the sky, until it's gone. And the sky is quiet again.

Now imagine a small candle, glowing softly in a dark, quiet room. Its light is warm and steady. It lights only a small circle around it. Just enough. You don't need to see the whole room. You don't need to see tomorrow. Just this small, warm circle of light, right here, right now.

Breathe in slowly. And as you breathe out, let the day go a little more. Whatever happened today, whatever you remember, or misremember, it doesn't need to be solved tonight. Your memories will be quietly sorted while you sleep. You can trust that process. You can let go.

And if tomorrow feels uncertain, that's alright. Remember the lantern in the misty forest. You don't need to see the whole path. You only need to see the next step. And right now, the next step is simply to rest.

Let your forehead soften. Let the small muscles around your eyes relax. Let your jaw loosen, just a little. Let your tongue rest gently. Let your shoulders fall away from your ears. With each breath out, let your body sink just a little deeper into stillness.

Your brain will keep working gently through the night. It will keep your heart beating and your breath flowing. It will sort your memories and tidy up the day. You don't need to supervise it. You can simply let go, and trust it to take care of you.
Breathe in. And out. Slowly. Calmly. There's nothing to remember. Nothing to plan. Nothing to explain. Just the soft rhythm of your breath, and the quiet comfort of resting.

Let's take one more slow journey through the body. Bring your attention to your feet. Let them be heavy and warm. Then your ankles. Your calves. Your knees. Let each part soften as you notice it, as if a gentle wave of warmth is moving slowly upward.

Now your hips, and your lower back. Let them sink. Your belly rises and falls with each breath. Your chest is soft. Your arms are heavy. Your hands are open and still. There is nothing to hold on to. Everything can rest.

Imagine you're lying beside that quiet moonlit lake again. The water is perfectly still. The air is cool and soft. Somewhere far away, a night bird calls once, and then everything is quiet. The moon's reflection floats on the water, calm and silver.

Your brain, the great storyteller, can tell you one last gentle story tonight. A story where you are safe, and warm, and completely at ease. Where the day is finished, and tomorrow can wait. Let yourself believe this story. It's a kind one.
Breathe in slowly. Hold it for just a moment. And breathe out, long and soft. Once more. In. And out. Let each breath carry you a little further toward sleep. Deeper. Softer. Quieter.

If your mind wanders back to anything from tonight, the gorilla, the dress, the chicken shed, just smile at it, and let it float away. It was only a story. You don't need to keep it. Let it drift, like a leaf on slow water, further and further away.

The room around you is quiet. Your body is heavy and warm. Your breath is slow and even. Your brain is gently turning down its lights, one by one, like a house at the end of a long day. Let the last lights dim. Let everything be still.
You are safe. You are resting. There is nothing more to do today. Just breathe, slowly, and let sleep come to you, in its own time, gently, like the tide coming in on a calm night.

Tomorrow, we'll explore something we all do every single day, often without noticing. Waiting. Why a minute in a queue can feel like an hour, and why some waits feel so much worse than others. But that's for tomorrow. For now, rest well. Goodnight.
